eyebrow: A different engine, not a flag
code:
Standard Spark execution:
  JVM, row-at-a-time, one row through each operator at a time

Photon execution:
  native C++, vectorized -- a batch of rows per operator call,
  using CPU instructions the JVM can't reach directly
caption: Photon replaces the execution engine for supported operators.

steps.label: SCANS & AGGREGATIONS
steps.sub: the biggest wins -- large row counts, decompression, GROUP BY

steps.label: JOINS
steps.sub: shuffle and broadcast joins vectorize well under Photon

steps.label: PYTHON UDFs
steps.sub: can't be vectorized -- falls back to plain JVM execution

code:
Query profile -> individual operator nodes
  [lightning-bolt icon] = this operator ran on Photon
  (no icon)             = this operator ran on plain JVM Spark

Cluster config checkbox says Photon is ON --
the query profile says which operators actually used it.
caption: Check the query profile, not the cluster settings screen.

subtitle: Re-optimizing the plan itself, at runtime.
